subject: How to suppress initial postgresqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) error with Shiny

messages.author: ef27ec9204e3a664
messages.subject: How to suppress initial postgresqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) error with Shiny
parts:
Dear collective intelligence,

I am querying some data and displaying the result using Shiny

This is from server.R:

 output$my_name <- renderUI({
        qry <- "select name from my_data ORDER BY name"
        rs = dbSendQuery(con,qry)
        mydata <- fetch(rs,n=-1)

        print('in fn 2')
        selectInput("mystuff", "", tryCatch(mydata$name))

    })


this is from ui.R:

uiOutput("my_name")

This outputs a beautiful dropbox populated with names, but first it gives me the following postgressDB error:

Error in postgresqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) :
  RS-DBI driver: (could not Retrieve the result : ERROR:  invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x82
)

Twice.

I can't figure out why I get this error and how to suppress it.  It's generated sometime after I retrieve data and before I output to screen.  The error flashes on screen before the next bit of data that uses "my_name" is used.
Anyone has encountered this before?

Thanks a lot!
-b

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: How to suppress initial postgresqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) error with Shiny
parts:
It sounds like there is data in your database that isn't UTF-8 encoded, yet you're accessing the database in a way that implies UTF-8 encoding. Or perhaps the table is actually marked as UTF-8 encoded but contains invalid data. I don't know Postgres well enough to tell you how to go about figuring that out.

If you have Shiny 0.8 installed you might be able to figure it out by setting this option before running your app:

options(shiny.error=traceback)

or for a more hands-on approach:

options(shiny.error=recover)

messages.author: 55ef9f20d51f01b3
messages.subject: Re: How to suppress initial postgresqlExecStatement(conn, statement, ...) error with Shiny
parts:
This is an old thread but I stumbled upon the same issue today in shiny_0.12.2. It appears to be caused by uiOutput() initiating with a NULL value. It only occurs briefly, then it uses the default selected value. 

As a workaround, I solved it by adding

 if (is.null(input$mystuff)){
     return(NULL)
     } else

in every function that depends on the value. But it looks like a bug in either uiOutput or selectInput.

/Jens
